title: Split Into K Equal-Sum Groups
statement:
You get an array of positive integers nums and a number k. Can you split all of the numbers into exactly k non-empty groups so that every group has the same sum? Each number goes into exactly one group.

Return true if it can be done, otherwise false.

examples.why: The total is 18, so each group needs 6: [5, 1], [4, 2], [3, 3].
The total 18 divides by 3, but a group holding a 4 needs another 2, and there is none. A divisible total is not enough.
[3, 3] and [2, 2, 2]. Filling groups greedily in the given order puts 3 + 2 together and gets stuck at 5.

hints: First, what must every group sum to? When can you answer false right away?
Place the numbers one by one into k buckets, never letting a bucket go over the target. Back up when a number fits nowhere.
Sort descending so big numbers fail fast, and if a number does not work in one empty bucket, it will not work in any other empty bucket either: stop trying more of them.

explain.intuition:
Each group must sum to target = total / k, so the total has to divide evenly and no single number may exceed the target. After that it is a search: put each number into one of k buckets, never letting a bucket go over target, and back up when a number fits nowhere.

Two prunes make it fast. Placing the biggest numbers first makes dead ends show up early. And all empty buckets are interchangeable: if putting a number into one empty bucket failed, trying the next empty bucket would explore the exact same arrangements, so you skip it. For a guaranteed bound there is also a bitmask DP over which numbers are used, which runs in O(n · 2ⁿ).
steps: Compute total. If it is not divisible by k, return false. Let target = total / k.
Recurse on index i with an array of k bucket sums. At i = n every bucket is exactly full, so return true.
Try each bucket where bucket + nums[i] ≤ target: add, recurse, remove. Return true if any branch does.
After trying a bucket that was empty, stop: the other empty buckets would repeat the same search.
pitfalls: Stopping at the divisibility check. Example 2 has a divisible total and is still impossible.
Filling groups greedily without backtracking. Example 3 gets stuck if the first group takes 3 + 2.
Skipping the empty-bucket prune. Without it the search tries the same split k! times and times out on n = 16.

complexity.time: O(kⁿ) worst case for the search, O(n · 2ⁿ) for the bitmask DP
complexity.space: O(n) for the search, O(2ⁿ) for the DP

solutions.title: Fill k buckets with backtracking
solutions.idea: Place numbers largest first into buckets that stay within the target; skip duplicate empty buckets.
solutions.time: O(kⁿ) worst case, fast in practice

solutions.title: Bitmask DP over used numbers
solutions.idea: For each subset of used numbers, store how full the current group is (sum mod target). A number can be added if it does not overflow the current group.

followups: Return the actual groups, not just true or false.
Why is it enough for the DP to store one fill level per subset, instead of the full contents of every group?
lcTitle: Partition to K Equal Sum Subsets
